A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KinMo work and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices A–G.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, generation, editing, trajectory-control, ablation, and user-study results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds human and LLM evaluations of annotation quality in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, hierarchical alignment, Motion Reasoner, coarse-to-fine generator, and editing/control procedures are retained. Wording revisions do not establish algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HumanML3D-derived KinMo data and retrieval, generation, editing, and trajectory-control scenarios. The new audit examines existing annotations without adding a dataset, domain, or motion scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every matched benchmark, ablation, and user study. MotionFix is newly cited but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a separate annotation audit involving five independent raters and 500 randomly selected samples, with three criteria scored from 0–10 and complementary GPT-4o-mini scoring. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new annotation-quality analysis directly examines spatial accuracy, temporal coherence, and consistency with global descriptions. Existing component ablations, training analyses, and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 20 evaluations with 95% confidence intervals in Table 2 and the same inference-seed statement. The annotation audit reports averages and bad-response rates without introducing uncertainty estimates or repeated-run procedures.

E6.justification: v3 Table 7 adds human mean scores of 8.24, 8.01, and 8.71 and LLM means of 8.30, 8.12, and 8.55, alongside bad-response rates. All matched pre-existing quantitative results and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: v3 Table 7 newly defines Bad Response Rate as the fraction of items scoring below 5. The motion-representation definitions, equations, rigid-body assumption, and Proposition 1 proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and claims about retrieval, generation, editing, and control retain their scope. The abstract's added scalability and cost-efficiency emphasis reflects automated, low-cost annotation already described in v2 Appendix B.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets the annotation audit as direct evidence of reliable spatial and temporal descriptions beyond indirect downstream metrics. Existing description-quality, short-transition, and rigid-body limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The conclusion changes the reported dataset-release status from a planned release to public availability. Existing annotation-cost and model-training details are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify live access.

R1.justification: v3 adds MotionFix, the FID source, and several diffusion and gesture references, while removing MMComposition, latent-diffusion, and VideoGrain references. The central positioning around kinematic descriptions remains stable.

P1.justification: Sentence-level copyediting, terminology and cross-reference corrections accompany revised author information and new acknowledgements. Former Appendix D.5 is merged into D.4, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the annotation-evaluation table, revises captions, and shifts some appendix table and text placement. Existing figures and the general table designs and two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The independent annotation audit in Appendix B and Table 7 provides direct quality evidence beyond v2's prompt-development checks and downstream results. This strengthens support for the dataset contribution, alongside clearer prose and reported public availability. The gain remains limited because the main experiments are unchanged and the audit's scoring and aggregation details are incomplete.
